files_read: tests/orders/*.json (header, depot, fleet blocks, and a whole-corpus scan for non-integer numerals)
files_not_read_in_full: solution/search/sisr.py: not executed by solve.sh or the verifier (solve.sh:24-28 only copies static plans), so its seeding cannot affect grading
environment/app/planner/plan_morning.py: candidate-side starting code, never run by the verifier (test_outputs.py:1-7, 17-32)
solution/plans/*.json: static data; their byte content is fixed by the manifest hashes
input_completeness.notes: Manifest hashes show tests/check_plan.py == environment/app/tools/check_plan.py, tests/orders/*.json == environment/app/orders/*.json, and tests/targets.json == environment/app/orders/targets.json (packet-manifest.json:12-19 vs 29-34).

coverage_sweep.random_seeds_and_generated_cases: No randomness in grading. The verifier reads four fixed plan files and evaluates them against fixed, sealed orders and targets (tests/test_outputs.py:19-48). The only random value is mktemp's RUN_DIR (tests/test.sh:13-14), used only as a cwd and never compared or read; pattern D-3, None.
coverage_sweep.clock_and_time: No wall-clock use. All times are integer seconds taken from the orders (tests/check_plan.py:70-95; tests/orders/harbour-lanes.json:6-7).
coverage_sweep.numeric_stability: All arithmetic is integer: distance uses math.isqrt with an exact ceiling (tests/check_plan.py:40-43); a scan of every tests/orders/*.json for decimal or exponent numerals found none; fleet pace/fixed/per_unit/shift/range are integers (tests/orders/old-town.json:1116-1140); depart must be a JSON int (tests/check_plan.py:70). Cost <= target is an exact integer comparison (tests/test_outputs.py:48) with targets equal to the reference costs (tests/targets.json:1-6, solution/solve.sh:18-22). No float tolerance edge.
coverage_sweep.ordering: Routes and stops are processed in plan order, which the contract defines as visiting order (dispatch-rules.md:33-35, 58-60). Set/dict iteration affects only error-message text (check_plan.py:21, 101-106), not pass/fail.
coverage_sweep.dependencies_and_network: Both images are pinned by digest (environment/Dockerfile:1, tests/Dockerfile:1); pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2 are pinned (tests/Dockerfile:3). The verifier runs with no network (task.toml:18-21). -p no:randomly and -p no:cacheprovider (tests/test.sh:15) remove test-order and cache effects.
coverage_sweep.timing_and_readiness: No services, sleeps or timeouts in the grading path. Evaluation is a linear pass over at most a few hundred customers per morning, far below verifier timeout_sec=1800 (task.toml:19).
coverage_sweep.environment_isolation: environment_mode = separate (task.toml:20); the verifier uses only its own copies of rules/orders/targets and runs no candidate code (test_outputs.py:1-7, 17-26), so edits to /app/tools or /app/orders cannot vary the grade between runs.
coverage_sweep.reference_path: solve.sh copies fixed plans and runs the checker (solution/solve.sh:24-28); no search or seed runs at oracle time, so oracle reward is reproducible.
coverage_sweep.reward_channel: reward.txt is initialized to 0 and set to 1 only on pytest rc==0 (tests/test.sh:4-5, 16-21); deterministic mapping.

interaction_sweep: Checked environment-variable override DISPATCH_PLANS (tests/test_outputs.py:19): unset by test.sh and the verifier image, so the default /app/plans path is used on every run. Checked the WORKDIR guard (tests/test.sh:7-11) against tests/Dockerfile:6 (WORKDIR /tests): always passes. Checked strict JSON loading (check_plan.py:18-37): repeated keys, NaN/Infinity and malformed input fail the same way every run. No interaction between the mutable candidate environment and grading was found.
non_blocking_observations: Transitive pytest dependencies (pluggy, iniconfig, packaging) are not pinned in tests/Dockerfile:3. They resolve once at image build and do not plausibly change the outcome of these eight pure-data assertions, so this is not reported as a finding.
reach_and_flip_summary: No uncontrolled input (seed, clock, remote data, filesystem order, timing) reaches a graded decision. A fixed submission gets the same eight verdicts on every clean run: the reference passes all eight and a fixed infeasible or over-target plan fails the same tests each time.
